text:
alex: Heads-up — found a kernel-picker flip that spikes latency on causal runs for head_dim=17 :confused:

alex: Minimal repro: seq_len=512, batch=4, head_dim=17, model=redwood/open-7b-8k-v3 (int8). Runtime is choosing flashv3_causal over sdpa_v2 and we're seeing a 2x p99 regression.

maria: Can you paste the exact command / logs so we can repro locally?

alex: Sure, here's the script I used and the selector dump: 
```bash
python -m runtime.bench --model redwood/open-7b-8k-v3 --seq_len 512 --batch 4 --head_dim 17 --precision int8 --causal true
```

Selector log excerpt: 
```
kernel_picker: features={seqlen_bucket=512-1024, head_unaligned=true, batch=4, arch=sm90, kv_cache_prefetch=on}
kernel_scores: sdpa_v2=0.52, flashv3_causal=0.48 -> selected flashv3_causal
measured_estimates: flashv3_est=8.7ms, sdpa_est=7.2ms
actual_profile: flashv3=12.3ms, sdpa=6.1ms
```

sam: oof. So the estimator thinks flashv3 is slightly worse, but the selector still chooses it? looks like some other weighting is beating the raw estimate (maybe a latency vs throughput score).

alex: Right — digging in, the score formula uses a linear combination of estimated_latency and a "compatibility" bonus when head_unaligned=false. For head_dim=17 head_unaligned=true, but somehow compatibility heuristics for causal kernels are giving flashv3 a small bonus. That bonus doesn't reflect the large memory-copy penalty we see on sm90 for non-aligned head dims.

jiang: sm90 has different shared memory behavior — unaligned head widths can trigger extra packing on flash kernels. Did you check KV-cache warmup? Could be prefetch penalties.

alex: I profiled warmup: first token passes show large memcpy hotspots and L2 thrash. KV warmup is fine for sdpa but flashv3's packing path creates a temp buffer per microbatch.

maria: Any quick mitigation we can flip on while we fix the selector weights? Maybe add hysteresis or prefer sdpa when the estimated gap < 10% and head_unaligned==true?

alex: I tried that patch locally. Patch logic: if head_unaligned and abs(est_flash - est_sdpa) < 0.10 * est_sdpa then prefer sdpa. Results: p99 went from 115ms -> 62ms on our microbench. Patch snippet: 
```diff
- if score_flash > score_sdpa: pick flash
+ if head_unaligned and est_diff_rel < 0.10: pick sdpa
+ elif score_flash > score_sdpa: pick flash
```

sam: Please put that behind a feature flag and add a small microbench. Also let's not hardcode 10% — we should parametrize by arch (sm80 vs sm90 vs arm64).

perf-bot: Perf upload: https://perf.internal/reports/3337771111
Summary (microbench model redwood/open-7b-8k-v3, seq=512, batch=4, head=17): pre-patch p50=22ms p95=98ms p99=115ms, post-patch p50=21ms p95=44ms p99=62ms.

jiang: I'll review and propose a per-arch LUT for the selector. We should also add a probe that measures a short microkernel latency at startup for a couple of representative (head_dim, seqlen) combos and feed that into the selector to avoid relying only on static estimates.

maria: Good idea — dynamic probing would adapt to platform peculiarities (thermal throttling or atypical memory bandwidth).

alex: Opening PR now with feature-flag + perf test + selector histogram logging. Assigning to @jiang for final review.

sam: Nice find, alex. cc perf infra to watch CI.

maria: :thumbsup:

jiang: I'll take it after lunch. Also adding a note to the autotune backlog to re-run tuning sweeps for flashv3 on sm90 with unaligned head widths.

alex: Thanks — I'll add the repro script and perf links to the PR description so QA can run it in their farms.
